item: UI — top fade on a conversation that never scrolls (2026-08-16)
branch: body.at-top is set by the RENDER path (maybeScroll) and by clearLogUI, not only by the scroll handler
provenance: User report 2026-08-16 (screenshot): `/model` on a NEW conversation drew its stdout greyed and apparently struck through — not a text style, but #fade-top's 18px solid→transparent band crossing the first block (chat.css:162, hidden by `body.at-top #fade-top { opacity: 0 }`). body.at-top was toggled only by the #log scroll handler and the two replay paths, so a log too short to scroll fires no scroll event and never hides the fade; local-command output is the one first block with no sticky .msg-user riding above the fade. Frame shape reused from fixture 47 (a bare whole-message `assistant` frame, measured 2026-08-15 on CLI 2.1.233) — this fixture asserts only what the RENDERER must do with a block it is given, never what the CLI emits. The at-top class is removed in each setup on purpose: the assertion must prove the render path RESTORES it, independently of whatever the previous fixture left on <body>. The two computed-opacity assertions await 250ms on purpose: #fade-top transitions opacity over .12s, so an unsettled read measures whatever the animation happens to be part-way through and passes or fails by timing alone (observed both ways 2026-08-16).

steps.note: a block rendered into a fresh, unscrollable log hides the top fade — the reported repro

expect.why: GUARD: the block drew at all — green in both phases
GUARD: the log is too short to scroll, so no scroll event ever fires — the premise
DISCRIMINATING: maybeScroll() now sets the toggle on every render (absent pre-fix)

DISCRIMINATING: the fade is actually painted away, not just class-toggled (is '1' pre-fix) Read after the .12s opacity transition (chat.css:164) has settled — an immediate getComputedStyle returns the PRE-transition value, which made this a coin flip: the same two runs failed it in step 1 and then in step 3.

steps.note: clearing the log (new conversation / resume / restart) leaves the fade hidden too

expect.why: GUARD: the log really was emptied
DISCRIMINATING: clearLogUI() calls updateTopFade() — an emptied log sits at the top (absent pre-fix)

steps.note: the toggle still discriminates: a log long enough to scroll keeps the fade visible
